**Test build for Nexo 1.2**: the **Emulator** now plays **Mega Drive / Genesis**, **PlayStation** and
**Nintendo 64** games too, next to SNES, with analog sticks and triggers. Everyone else stays on v1.1.0.

> **Hosts:** this needs the server from this test build too. Older servers refuse the new consoles and
> don't pass analog sticks on.

## New consoles

In a voice channel, click the **controller** button and pick the game file you own. Nexo tells the console
from the file:

| Console | Pick |
| --- | --- |
| SNES | `.sfc`, `.smc`, `.swc`, `.fig` or a `.zip` with one |
| Mega Drive / Genesis | `.md`, `.gen`, `.smd`, `.bin` or a `.zip` with one |
| Nintendo 64 | `.z64`, `.n64`, `.v64` or a `.zip` with one |
| PlayStation | the `.cue` **together with all its `.bin` files** (select them all at once), or a `.chd`, `.pbp`, `.iso` or `.img` |

If Nexo can't tell (a `.bin` without a `.cue`), it asks which console it is.

- **Mega Drive:** 6-button pads, and 4 players in games made for the 4-player adapters.
- **PlayStation:** no BIOS needed: Nexo has a built-in replacement that runs most games. If you own a
  PlayStation BIOS file, pick it together with the game for the best compatibility. 4 players work through
  the multitap.
- **Nintendo 64:** analog stick, C buttons on the right stick, and 4 controllers.

Nexo doesn't provide games or BIOS files. The files stay on your computer.

## Controllers

- Analog sticks now reach the game on PlayStation and Nintendo 64, from the host and from friends.
- Triggers are **L2 / R2** (keyboard **U / O**), clicking the sticks is **L3 / R3** (keyboard **F / G**).
- **Show controls** next to the controllers lists what each button does on the game's console.
- On a keyboard the arrows move the N64 control stick. On PlayStation they're the d-pad, so games that need
  the analog stick need a gamepad.

## What to test

- **Nintendo 64** is the least proven: does your game show its 3D graphics correctly, and does it run at
  full speed? Short stutters right after it starts are expected. Tell us which games break.
- **PlayStation:** do your discs boot without a BIOS? Do the sticks feel right?
- **Mega Drive:** 6-button fighting games, and 4-player games.
- **Saves:** in-game saves (memory cards, cartridge saves) aren't kept when the game closes yet, so use
  **Quick save**.

## Leaving test builds

Already on a test build? Nothing to do: Nexo updates itself. To go back to the regular releases:
**Settings → App → Updates → Leave test builds**, then restart Nexo.
